classification.difficultyReason: Read a one-unit horizontal or vertical translation from each circle equation, retain the unit radius, and identify the axis intercepts, including tangency at the origin.

content.prompt: Sketch each circle by shifting $x^2+y^2=1$ either horizontally or vertically. Mark all intercepts with the axes.

answer.worked: Shift the unit circle right 1 unit. Its centre becomes $(1,0)$ and its radius remains $1$. It touches the $y$-axis at $(0,0)$ and crosses the $x$-axis at $(0,0)$ and $(2,0)$.

spec.description: Unit circle shifted right one unit, with both axis-intercept locations labelled.

answer.worked: Shift the unit circle up 1 unit. Its centre becomes $(0,1)$ and its radius remains $1$. It touches the $x$-axis at $(0,0)$ and crosses the $y$-axis at $(0,0)$ and $(0,2)$.

spec.description: Unit circle shifted up one unit, with its axis intercepts labelled outside the circle.

answer.worked: Shift the unit circle down 1 unit. Its centre becomes $(0,-1)$ and its radius remains $1$. It touches the $x$-axis at $(0,0)$ and crosses the $y$-axis at $(0,0)$ and $(0,-2)$.

spec.description: Unit circle shifted down one unit, with origin and lower y-intercept labelled.

answer.worked: Shift the unit circle left 1 unit. Its centre becomes $(-1,0)$ and its radius remains $1$. It touches the $y$-axis at $(0,0)$ and crosses the $x$-axis at $(-2,0)$ and $(0,0)$.

spec.description: Unit circle shifted left one unit, with intercepts at x=−2 and the origin.
